TheBasement

Sixteen inches taken out from under a standing house, hauled up the stairs on a cart and a cable. Then a floor built back on gravel and foam, and a room to train in.

09 – 25 Feb 2025

Breaking the slab

An electric breaker on four inches of floor. It comes up in plates and the plates go up the carpeted stairs in a milk crate. Upstairs is still a house.

17 – 28 Feb 2025

First loads out

Nothing leaves this basement except by hand and up the stairs.

07 Mar 2025

Bare walls

The foundation stands uncovered well below the old floor line. Nothing was ever put under it. The walls sit on their footings and stayed there the whole way down.

Mar – Jun 2025

The haul line

A cart on timber rails, a cable, and a winch chained across the truck box. The stairs stop being stairs. Dates here are bracketed by the dated files on either side.

18 May – 24 Jun 2025

Under the house

Working depth reached for the first time, with the mechanical left standing on its own.

24 Jun 2025 → 08 Mar 2026

The water

Spring 2025 it rained hard and the house was not set up for it. Water came in and contaminated the packed ground the floor was going to sit on. That ground had to leave. In the winter of 2026 the floor came down another six inches, to sixteen below the original, to get back to sound base. Neither the water nor the second dig was photographed — 257 days pass here with no files at all, and most of the 563 are this.

08 Mar 2026

Back to dirt, six inches lower

Sound ground again, sixteen inches below where the old floor sat. From here the floor gets built up rather than poured.

07 – 09 Apr 2026

Twenty yards of gravel

None of it came down the stairs.

10 Apr 2026

Poly and foam

Ten mil poly over the gravel, then half-inch DuroFoam wall to wall with every seam taped.

Apr 2026

23/32 subfloor over the foam, lines snapped, two layers thick.

Apr – 20 Jul 2026

The room

Banners on the concrete, mats over the board, rings off the joists.

26 Aug 2026

The shop, still open

The other half of the basement. Subfloor down and unlined, benches and saws working.

undated

What it did

No capture dates in these three. File numbering puts all of them after June 2025. What a photograph can report here is composition and muscle — bone, tendon and coordination do not show up in it.

What the record doesn't hold

  • Hours. Never counted, and a guess would be worse than the blank.
  • What the poly cost.
  • The second dig. Six inches came out and nothing was photographed.
  • The water itself, and how far into the house it got.
